scope: Current jump/fall generation, not Frame Animation V2
actual_input_prompt: The character performs one small jump and returns to the starting stance, maintaining the same three-quarter right-facing view. Only the arms and legs change pose: slight knee bend, knees tuck, legs extend, then land. Keep the head still and preserve the input face throughout: identical open eyes, eye whites, pupils, jaw outline and skin colors, with no expression change. Animate the poses without moving the whole character upward across the canvas.
returned_final_prompt: The young man in the yellow hoodie and dark pants performs a small vertical jump while keeping his head completely still in a three-quarter right-facing view. His knees bend slightly before tucking inward, then his legs extend downward to land on the ground. Throughout the entire hop, his facial expression remains unchanged and the character sprite does not shift upward across the canvas.
optimized_prompt_source: Prior CLI tool output, no new API read
face_tolerance: User accepts small changes; raw generated faces retained
workflow_order_correction: First: direct animation from initial reference, confirmed by user. Later: pose preparation, keyframe animation and local frame repair attempts. Latest: regenerate from original side idle and select frames. Exact order of every later step is not inferred.
acceptance_standard: Usable game art at actual game scale: stable character recognition, natural action and consistent style. Small pixel, color or shape variations are acceptable.
strict_edit_assessment: Both jobs succeeded. Their full outputs were rejected under an overly strict outside-eye pixel-change criterion and were not independently validated in-game. Pixel counts alone do not establish unusability or a Meowa defect.
